title: Genotype-Informed Interaction Landscape of the Dengue Envelope Glycoprotein with Host Cellular Proteins: Structural Dynamics, Thermodynamic Cooperativity, and Binding Specificity
authors: Daniel Ferreira de Lima Neto; Juan Philippe Teixeira; Marcus Alexandre Finzi Corat; Miklos Maximiliano Bajay; Gustavo Henrique Goulart Trossini; Daniel Santos Mansur; Elcio de Souza Leal; Luiz Mario Ramos Janini; Caio Cesar de Melo Freire
one_liner_zh: 该文研究登革病毒包膜蛋白与宿主蛋白的互作网络，采用分子对接、MD和MM/GBSA，但对象为病毒蛋白-宿主蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，方法虽可迁移但非TF-DNA体系，故评分较低。
abstract: 1 Abstract Dengue virus (DENV) entry has historically been viewed as a receptor-centric process in which viral envelope proteins engage isolated host factors to initiate infection. However, mounting evidence reveals that viral attachment, internalization, and intracellular trafficking occur within complex molecular environments where multiple interacting host proteins shape the infection landscape. Here we introduce vectorial host interaction fields—a framework that represents intermolecular contacts as directional vectors embedded within host protein interaction networks, providing structural and systems-level insight into viral entry. Docking analyses were performed across sixteen dengue envelope genotype variants, whereas molecular dynamics and MM/GBSA analyses were conducted on representative complexes selected from this genotype-informed screening. We characterized dengue envelope interactions with thirteen host proteins involved in membrane attachment, receptor signaling, cytoskeletal transport, vesicular trafficking, proteostasis, and immune regulation. Our multiscale approach integrated protein–protein docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations of representative complexes, MM/GBSA binding free energy analysis, and vectorial hydrogen-bond formalism encoding orientation, persistence, and angular entropy. We identified four recurrent viral interface architectures: multivalent anchoring (BiP/GRP78, Betaglycan), electrostatic sliding (Glypican-1), focal regulation (Claudin-1, SUMO), and conserved cytoskeletal modules (Actin, Rab5). Ternary docking analyses revealed that viral stability is strongly conditioned by local network context, with conditional ΔΔ G values ranging from approximately −3.4 to +6.9 kcal mol −1 depending on neighboring proteins and assembly sequence. These findings support a systems-level model of dengue entry driven by layered host interaction fields rather than a single dominant receptor, but they should be interpreted as computational structural hypotheses requiring biochemical, biophysical, and cellular validation. Detailed structural datasets, molecular dynamics trajectories, vectorial analyses, and per-residue MM/GBSA decomposition are provided in the companion Supplementary Material, which includes extended Results and Discussion, comprehensive Limitations assessment, and VectorPROT pipeline documentation supporting these findings.
abstract_zh: 1 摘要 登革病毒（Dengue virus, DENV）的进入历来被视为一个以受体为中心的过程，其中病毒包膜蛋白与孤立的宿主因子结合以启动感染。然而，越来越多的证据表明，病毒附着、内化和细胞内运输发生在复杂的分子环境中，多种相互作用的宿主蛋白共同塑造了感染格局。在此，我们引入矢量宿主相互作用场（vectorial host interaction fields）——一个将分子间接触表示为嵌入宿主蛋白相互作用网络中的方向性矢量的框架，为病毒进入提供结构和系统层面的见解。我们对十六种登革包膜基因型变体进行了对接分析，而分子动力学和MM/GBSA分析则针对从该基因型知情筛选中选出的代表性复合物进行。我们表征了登革包膜与十三种宿主蛋白的相互作用，这些蛋白涉及膜附着、受体信号传导、细胞骨架运输、囊泡运输、蛋白质稳态和免疫调节。我们的多尺度方法整合了蛋白质-蛋白质对接、代表性复合物的200 ns分子动力学模拟、MM/GBSA结合自由能分析，以及编码方向性、持久性和角度熵的矢量氢键形式。我们识别出四种反复出现的病毒界面架构：多价锚定（BiP/GRP78、Betaglycan）、静电滑动（Glypican-1）、局部调控（Claudin-1、SUMO）和保守细胞骨架模块（Actin、Rab5）。三元对接分析揭示，病毒稳定性强烈受局部网络背景影响，条件性ΔΔG值根据邻近蛋白和组装顺序约为−3.4至+6.9 kcal mol⁻¹。这些发现支持一个由分层宿主相互作用场驱动的登革进入的系统级模型，而非单一主导受体，但应将其解释为计算结构假设，需通过生化、生物物理和细胞验证。详细的结构数据集、分子动力学轨迹、矢量分析以及逐残基MM/GBSA分解在随附的补充材料中提供，其中包括扩展的结果与讨论、全面的局限性评估以及支持这些发现的VectorPROT管道文档。
